answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies prices identity instead of trusting it. Every agent must post a bond before submitting work: stake locked to a key, slashed when duplicate or fabricated submissions are proven. Stake is scarce, so a thousand puppets lock a thousand times the minimum, and cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays once. Reputation decays without real settlements, so farming cannot compound. The defence is that burn rate: an operator launching a whole voyage of fake agents pays docking per shell on the knoll, until only one orchard of genuine keys stays solvent.
